questions.stem: KHARIF crops in India are sown in:

options.option_text: JUNE-JULY (with the onset of SW monsoon) + harvested in SEPT-OCT; includes rice, maize, bajra, jowar, cotton, sugarcane, tur

questions.explanation: AGRICULTURAL SEASONS in India: (1) KHARIF (monsoon) — sown June-July with SW monsoon arrival; harvested SEPT-OCT; water-intensive crops; includes PADDY/RICE (dominant), MAIZE, JOWAR (sorghum), BAJRA (pearl millet), RAGI (finger millet), GROUNDNUT, COTTON, SUGARCANE, SOYABEAN, TUR (arhar/pigeon pea), URAD, MOONG, JUTE. (2) RABI (winter) — sown OCT-NOV (post-monsoon, using soil moisture + winter rains); harvested MARCH-APRIL; includes WHEAT (dominant), BARLEY, GRAM/CHANA, MUSTARD/RAPESEED, PEAS, LENTIL/MASOOR, LINSEED, ONION, POTATO. (3) ZAID (summer) — sown MARCH-APRIL, harvested MAY-JUNE; short-duration crops; WATERMELON, MUSKMELON, CUCUMBER, VEGETABLES, MOONG, FODDER CROPS. MSP (Minimum Support Price): announced for 23 crops (14 Kharif + 6 Rabi + others) by CACP recommendations, approved by CCEA. NAMES: Kharif from Arabic 'autumn' (these crops ready in autumn); Rabi from Arabic 'spring' (harvested in spring). TOP RICE STATES: WB, UP, Punjab, AP, Telangana, Bihar, TN. TOP WHEAT STATES: UP, Punjab, Haryana, MP, Rajasthan. MP has surpassed Punjab in wheat production recently. INDIA is the 2nd largest producer globally of rice + wheat (China is 1st for rice; China 1st, India 2nd wheat). LARGEST producer of PULSES + MILK + SPICES + JUTE globally.

questions.stem: The 'GREEN REVOLUTION' in India, launched in the 1960s-70s, primarily increased the production of:

options.option_text: WHEAT + RICE — through HYVs (High-Yielding Varieties), fertilisers, irrigation, MSP; concentrated in Punjab, Haryana, W. UP

questions.explanation: GREEN REVOLUTION — transformation of Indian agriculture from 1965-66 onwards; made India from 'ship-to-mouth' food importer to self-sufficient + exporter. DRIVERS: (1) HYV SEEDS — especially high-yielding wheat varieties developed by NORMAN BORLAUG (Nobel Peace Prize 1970) at CIMMYT Mexico, brought to India in 1965; Indian scientist MS SWAMINATHAN adapted them (Sonora-64, Lerma Rojo); (2) CHEMICAL FERTILISERS (urea, DAP, potash); (3) PESTICIDES + herbicides; (4) IRRIGATION infrastructure (Bhakra Nangal, tube wells); (5) MECHANISATION (tractors, harvesters, threshers); (6) MSP + procurement via FCI (1965 establishment) + state mandis; (7) INSTITUTIONAL CREDIT (bank nationalisation 1969, NABARD 1982). GEOGRAPHIC CONCENTRATION: PUNJAB, HARYANA, Western UP — became 'WHEAT BOWL'. Rice component later in AP, TN, Punjab. KEY CROPS: WHEAT (fastest growth), RICE. OTHER revolutions followed: (a) WHITE Revolution — MILK — Verghese Kurien + Amul's OPERATION FLOOD (1970s-90s); India now world's LARGEST milk producer. (b) YELLOW Revolution — OILSEEDS — 1986-90. (c) BLUE Revolution — FISH — 1985 onwards. (d) PINK Revolution — MEAT + POULTRY; or alternatively prawns/shrimps. (e) SILVER Revolution — eggs. (f) RAINBOW Revolution — holistic agri-growth. CRITIQUES: bypassed dryland farmers + pulses + millets; caused GROUNDWATER depletion (Punjab); soil degradation; fertiliser overuse; regional inequality. M.S. SWAMINATHAN ('Father of Indian Green Revolution') died 2023; Bharat Ratna 2024.

questions.stem: Match the crop with its LARGEST PRODUCER (state) in India (2022-23 data): (1) SUGARCANE; (2) COTTON; (3) TEA; (4) COFFEE.

options.option_text: Bihar; Tamil Nadu; West Bengal; Tamil Nadu

questions.explanation: LARGEST PRODUCING STATES (commercial + plantation crops): (1) SUGARCANE — UTTAR PRADESH (≈45% of national production); followed by Maharashtra + Karnataka + TN. UP grows it in the GANGETIC PLAINS; Maharashtra + Karnataka use it more intensively for sugar + ethanol. India = world's 2nd largest sugarcane producer (Brazil 1st). Sugarcane is INDIA's 2nd most important cash crop (after cotton). (2) COTTON — GUJARAT (≈33%); followed by Maharashtra + Telangana. 'White gold'; India is the world's LARGEST cotton producer (above China). BT COTTON (GM) widely cultivated. COTTON BELT: Kharif crop of black cotton soil (regur). (3) TEA — ASSAM (≈50% of national production, world's LARGEST tea-growing region); also grown in West Bengal (Darjeeling), Tamil Nadu (Nilgiris), Kerala (Munnar), HP (Kangra). India = world's 2nd largest tea producer (China 1st); LARGEST CONSUMER per capita; DARJEELING tea has GI tag. Introduced by British in 1820s (Assam). (4) COFFEE — KARNATAKA (≈70%! Chikmagalur, Coorg, Hassan); also Kerala (Wayanad) + TN (Nilgiris). India = world's 7th largest coffee producer. ARABICA + ROBUSTA grown. OTHER crops: (5) RICE — West Bengal; (6) WHEAT — UP; (7) PULSES — MP; (8) OILSEEDS — MP/Rajasthan; (9) GROUNDNUT — Gujarat; (10) RAPESEED/MUSTARD — Rajasthan; (11) SOYABEAN — MP; (12) JUTE — West Bengal (≈80%); (13) RUBBER — Kerala (≈75%); (14) SILK — Karnataka (mulberry); (15) SPICES — Kerala/Gujarat; (16) COCONUT — Kerala/TN.

questions.stem: The BLACK COTTON SOIL (REGUR) is best suited for COTTON cultivation. It is MAINLY found in:

options.option_text: DECCAN TRAP region — Maharashtra, MP, Gujarat, Karnataka, AP; derived from basalt + volcanic lava

questions.explanation: BLACK COTTON SOIL / REGUR — a residual black soil derived from DECCAN TRAPS (weathered BASALT + volcanic lava of Cretaceous age). COVERS ~16% of India's geographic area. DISTRIBUTION: MAHARASHTRA (largest area), MADHYA PRADESH, GUJARAT, KARNATAKA (northern), ANDHRA PRADESH (western), TAMIL NADU (Coimbatore, Salem), Chhattisgarh (parts). CHARACTERISTICS: (1) RICH in calcium, potassium, magnesium, iron, lime; POOR in nitrogen, phosphorus, humus. (2) Very FINE TEXTURE → retains moisture well (good for dry Kharif crops under rain-fed conditions). (3) Develops DEEP CRACKS in summer (self-ploughing) + swells when wet → can damage foundations, roads. (4) Deep black → absorbs heat, warms soil fast. (5) DARK COLOUR from titanium + iron compounds. SUITABLE CROPS: COTTON (primary), wheat, jowar, linseed, pulses, tobacco, sugarcane, soyabean, groundnut, sunflower. SIX MAJOR INDIAN SOIL TYPES (ICAR classification): (1) ALLUVIAL (~40% — Indo-Gangetic plain, coastal plains; most fertile; khadar + bhangar subtypes); (2) BLACK/Regur; (3) RED + YELLOW (peninsular India, derived from metamorphic rocks); (4) LATERITE (areas of high rainfall + temp — Kerala, Karnataka, Odisha, hills of NE + Eastern + Western Ghats); (5) ARID/DESERT (Rajasthan, Gujarat); (6) FOREST/Mountain (Himalayan slopes). Other: Saline/Alkaline (Punjab's reh); Peaty + Marshy (Kerala's Kuttanad, Sundarbans).

questions.stem: The 'WHITE REVOLUTION' (Operation Flood) that made India the world's LARGEST MILK PRODUCER was led by:

options.option_text: Dr VERGHESE KURIEN ('Father of White Revolution' / 'Milkman of India') via AMUL + NDDB from 1970

questions.explanation: OPERATION FLOOD / WHITE REVOLUTION — launched 13 January 1970 by the NATIONAL DAIRY DEVELOPMENT BOARD (NDDB, est. 1965, Anand, Gujarat). ARCHITECT: Dr VERGHESE KURIEN (1921-2012) — 'Milkman of India' / 'Father of the White Revolution'; Founder-Chairman of NDDB (1965); Founding Chairman of AMUL (Anand Milk Union Limited, est. 1946 by Tribhuvandas Patel). AMUL MODEL: 3-tier cooperative — (1) VILLAGE-level milk producers' societies; (2) DISTRICT-level unions (e.g., Kaira District Co-op Milk Producers' Union, AMUL); (3) STATE-level federations (Gujarat Co-op Milk Marketing Federation, GCMMF, markets the AMUL brand). Motto: 'farmer owned, farmer run'. 3 PHASES of Operation Flood (1970-96): Phase I (1970-80) — 18 milksheds, 'Anand Pattern' replicated; Phase II (1981-85) — Operation spread nationwide; Phase III (1985-96) — consolidation. RESULT: India surpassed USA as world's largest MILK producer in 1998; today ~24% of global milk. Per-capita milk availability: ~430 grams/day (2022) — above WHO minimum. KURIEN AWARDS: Padma Vibhushan (1999), World Food Prize (1989), Magsaysay Award (1963). HIS OTHER achievement: HE PIONEERED milk powder FROM BUFFALO milk (previously thought impossible; developed at Amul's Anand lab by engineers Dalaya + Kurien) — this made India's buffalo-heavy dairy viable. 26 NOVEMBER (Kurien's birthday) celebrated as NATIONAL MILK DAY.

questions.stem: INDIA's largest producer of PULSES is:

options.option_text: MADHYA PRADESH — ~25% of national production; gram (chana), tur, urad, moong, masoor; state gets 'Krishi Karman' Awards often

questions.explanation: PULSES — India is the WORLD'S LARGEST producer, consumer + importer of pulses. TOP STATES: (1) MADHYA PRADESH — ~25% of national output (3.5-5 MT/yr); main crops = GRAM/chana + tur/arhar + urad + moong + masoor. MP is also largest producer of SOYABEAN. (2) RAJASTHAN — ~17%; desert + semi-arid areas are pulse-friendly. (3) MAHARASHTRA — ~14%; tur heartland, Vidarbha. (4) UP — ~9%; (5) Karnataka, AP, Bihar follow. INDIA IMPORTS pulses despite being largest producer — demand outpaces supply due to rising population + vegetarianism + low productivity (~700-800 kg/ha vs Canada's 2,000+). MAJOR IMPORT sources: CANADA (yellow peas + lentils), Myanmar (urad/tur), Mozambique + Tanzania + Sudan + Malawi (tur); long-term deals signed with Mozambique. ICRISAT (Hyderabad) leads pulse research. NATIONAL PULSES MISSION + PM Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) for procurement. MSP hikes 2014-2024 (chana, tur, urad, moong, masoor). Pulses nitrogen-fix soil (legumes — Rhizobium bacteria) → sustainable. NATIONAL FOOD SECURITY Act 2013 covers pulse distribution via PDS in some states. INDIAN PULSES: CHANA (Cicer arietinum, gram), TUR/ARHAR (Cajanus cajan, pigeon pea), URAD (Vigna mungo, black gram), MOONG (Vigna radiata, green gram), MASOOR (Lens culinaris, red lentil), rajma (kidney bean), lobia (cowpea), matar (field pea). 2016 = International Year of Pulses (UN, proposed by India).

questions.stem: The MINIMUM SUPPORT PRICE (MSP) for agricultural crops is RECOMMENDED by:

options.option_text: CACP — Commission for Agricultural Costs + Prices (an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture); CCEA of Cabinet APPROVES it

questions.explanation: MSP (MINIMUM SUPPORT PRICE) — a guarantee-floor price by the Indian government to protect farmers from post-harvest price crash + incentivise production of target crops. PROCESS: (1) CACP (Commission for Agricultural Costs + Prices) — an attached office of Ministry of Agriculture + Farmers' Welfare (est. 1965 as APC, renamed CACP 1985). Recommends MSPs based on: A2 (paid-out costs), A2+FL (paid-out + imputed family labour), C2 (comprehensive cost incl. rent + interest on owned assets). (2) CACP submits PRICE POLICY REPORTS for Kharif + Rabi crops to the government. (3) CCEA (Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by PM) — APPROVES the MSPs. (4) FCI (Food Corporation of India, est. 1965) — the MAIN procurement agency for WHEAT + RICE; state agencies also procure in some states (Markfed in Punjab etc.). CROPS COVERED: 23 — 14 KHARIF (paddy, jowar, bajra, ragi, maize, tur/arhar, moong, urad, groundnut, sunflower seed, soyabean, sesamum, nigerseed, cotton) + 6 RABI (wheat, barley, gram, masoor, rapeseed/mustard, safflower) + 2 others (jute + copra) + sugarcane (FRP — Fair + Remunerative Price — by CCEA). SWAMINATHAN COMMISSION (2004-06): recommended MSP = C2 + 50%; partially implemented from 2018 as A2+FL + 50%. FARM LAW PROTESTS (2020-21): one key demand was LEGAL GUARANTEE of MSP; farm laws repealed Nov 2021; MSP committee set up 2022; recent 2024 protests continue. PROCUREMENT heavily skewed — WHEAT + RICE dominate; Punjab + Haryana farmers benefit most; pulse + oilseed procurement weaker.

questions.stem: The PM-KISAN SAMMAN NIDHI scheme provides INCOME SUPPORT to farmers of:

options.option_text: ALL landholding farmers — ₹6000/year in 3 installments of ₹2000 each — direct benefit transfer (DBT) to Aadhaar-linked accounts

questions.explanation: PM-KISAN SAMMAN NIDHI — CENTRAL-SECTOR scheme (100% Centre-funded) launched 1 FEBRUARY 2019 (Interim Budget), effective RETROSPECTIVELY from 1 DECEMBER 2018; 1st instalment disbursed Feb 24, 2019 by PM Modi at Gorakhpur. BENEFICIARIES (post-1 Jun 2019 expansion): ALL LANDHOLDING farming families (previously only <2ha holders); EXCLUSIONS: former + current constitutional post-holders; MPs/MLAs/MLCs; retired govt officials; income-tax payers in preceding year; pensioners >₹10000/month; professionals (doctors, lawyers, CAs); INSTITUTIONAL landholders. AMOUNT: ₹6000/year per family in 3 EQUAL INSTALMENTS of ₹2000 — April-July, Aug-Nov, Dec-March. DBT directly to bank accounts via AADHAAR-seeded banking (NPCI). BUDGET: ~₹60,000 crore/year; total ~9.5+ crore beneficiary farmers; launched via PM-KISAN portal (pmkisan.gov.in). RELATED farmer schemes: (1) PMFBY — Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (2016, crop insurance; premium 1.5-2% Kharif, Rabi); (2) PM-KMY — PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana (2019, pension scheme; ₹3000/month post-60); (3) Soil Health Card (2015); (4) e-NAM (National Agriculture Market, 2016, online mandi integration); (5) Kisan Credit Card (1998); (6) PM Matsya Sampada Yojana (fisheries 2020); (7) PMKSY — PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (irrigation 2015); (8) PDMC (Per Drop More Crop). STATE variants: Andhra PM-Kisan top-up (₹13,500); TELANGANA Rythu Bandhu (₹10,000/acre/year 2018); Odisha KALIA; WB Krishak Bandhu. DOUBLING FARMER INCOME — target for 2022 (goal partially met).

questions.stem: India is the LARGEST PRODUCER in the world of:

options.option_text: MILK, PULSES, JUTE, SPICES, COTTON — all 5 are world-#1 categories for India

questions.explanation: INDIA'S WORLD-#1 AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS (as of 2023 FAO + APEDA data): (1) MILK — #1, 24% of global; ~230 MT/yr. (2) PULSES — #1, 25% of global; ~27 MT/yr. (3) JUTE — #1, 55% of global; ~10 MT/yr (mostly WB). (4) SPICES — #1, 70% of production + consumption; major exports of chilli, turmeric, cumin, coriander, pepper; India is 'Spice Bowl of the World'. (5) COTTON — #1 in production as of 2015 (overtook China) — ~6-6.5 MT/yr. (6) BANANA — #1 by far, ~26% global. (7) MANGO — #1, 40% global (Alphonso, Dasheri, Langra, Chausa, Totapuri). (8) PAPAYA, CUSTARD APPLE, GUAVA, CHIKOO — #1. (9) CASHEW — #1 producer (historically; now China comes close). (10) CASTOR OIL — #1. (11) GINGER — #1. (12) OKRA — #1. (13) BUFFALO MEAT — #1. INDIA'S WORLD #2 products: WHEAT (after China), RICE (after China), SUGARCANE (after Brazil), ONION (after China), POTATO (after China), GROUNDNUT (after China), TEA (after China), FISH (after China), SILK (after China). #3: COFFEE in Robusta; TOBACCO. INDIA'S WORLD #1 CONSUMER of: tea, pulses, spices. INDIA'S LARGEST EXPORTS in agriculture: rice (basmati + non-basmati, #1 rice exporter globally — ~40% market share), sugar, buffalo meat, spices, cotton, tea. TOTAL AGRI EXPORTS ~$50 billion. KRISHI UDAN YOJANA + APEDA promote exports.

questions.stem: The 'SUGAR BOWL' of India refers to the belt of which state?

options.option_text: UTTAR PRADESH (especially the Ganges basin of the western + central UP — Muzaffarnagar, Meerut, Bijnor, Shahjahanpur, Sitapur belts)

questions.explanation: 'SUGAR BOWL OF INDIA' — nickname for UTTAR PRADESH, which accounts for ~45% of India's sugarcane production + ~35-40% of sugar production. MAIN SUGARCANE BELT: western UP districts — MUZAFFARNAGAR, MEERUT, BULANDSHAHR, BIJNOR, SAHARANPUR, BAGHPAT, SHAMLI; central UP — Bareilly, Shahjahanpur, Sitapur, Lakhimpur Kheri. Home to many of India's oldest sugar mills (Triveni, Bajaj Hindusthan, Balrampur Chini, DCM Shriram). NATURAL FAVORS: (1) fertile alluvial soil of Gangetic plain; (2) warm humid summers + mild winters; (3) abundant irrigation (Ganga, Yamuna canal systems, tubewells); (4) Ganga-Yamuna doab = one of world's most productive agricultural zones. TROPICAL vs SUBTROPICAL belts of sugarcane in India: (a) SUBTROPICAL = UP, BIHAR, PUNJAB, HARYANA, UTTARAKHAND — 60% of area but LOWER yield (~65 tonnes/ha); lower sucrose content. (b) TROPICAL = MAHARASHTRA, KARNATAKA, AP, TELANGANA, TAMIL NADU, GUJARAT — HIGHER yield (~85-100 tonnes/ha); higher sucrose (12%+); longer growing season. Despite lower area, TROPICAL belt has HIGHER productivity; Maharashtra + Karnataka contribute ~60% of India's SUGAR production (not cane). INDIA = world's 2nd-largest sugarcane producer + 2nd-largest sugar producer (Brazil leads). Sugarcane = a key source of BIOETHANOL (target 20% blending by 2025-26; currently ~12%). SUGAR MILL payments to farmers are a perennial political issue — state-level FRP + SAP differences.
